newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador on track to peg currency to dollar - Concha.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador on track to peg currency to dollar - Concha.

text.p: Ecuador's Finance Minister Pablo Concha said Monday Ecuador will introduce a fixed currency regime, pegging the sucre to the dollar.
Concha said on television that whatever else is in the economic plan that the Ecuadorean government will unveil Sunday, it will definitely include a convertibility plan.
He said the dollar would be set at no more than 4,000 sucres but did not specify the exact rate. It traded at 3,395 sucres Monday.

"I am completely sure from the evaluations we have carried out that the dollar will not be pegged above that level. We have still not decided on the parity, which will be the result of our projections and economic conditions," said Concha.
He went on to say "Convertibility is not just a monetary issue of the parity between the dollar and sucre, but a completely new system where a lot depends on fiscal discipline."
Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, the architect of Argentina's plan pegging the peso to the dollar at a one-to-one parity, is advising Ecuador's government.
Argentina's system obliges the central bank to hold 85 percent of cash dollar reserves, bonds, gold and other foreign currency reserves for every peso circulating in the economy.
Concha said various conditions, such as a stronger financial sector, more exports, changes in labor relations and institutional changes, will be needed for convertibility to work.
He added that through the rest of this year and in 1997, priority will be given to controlling state spending.
